transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-09-02 15:00 PDT | Duration: 45 min | Attendees: Jordan Liu, Priya Nair, Evan Park (Redwood)  Marcus Hale, Sofia Ortiz, Amir Khan, Tess Moreno (Granite Capital)

Summary: quick renewal/expansion check-in; discuss capacity increase, add eu-west region, confirm security docs and procurement next steps.

00:00 Jordan: hey all, thanks for taking the time. quick agenda  renewal timeline, capacity needs, regions, and any security or procurement blockers.
00:18 Marcus: yeah thanks, um so we've been happy overall, cost has been fine, but traffic spiked Q2 so we want to bump reserved capacity and add EU to reduce cross-region latency for our traders in london.
00:31 Priya: great, can you give rough numbers  qps or tokens per minute  so we can size the dedicated pool?
00:37 Sofia: sure, right now peak is about 1.2k reqs/min with avg 60 tokens per req; expected to double during earnings next month, and we want headroom for 3x.
00:49 Priya: ok that helps. quick note  for Dedicated we recommend a mix of smaller instances for burst plus steady pool, that gives better latency tail and cost.
01:05 Amir: security question  for Private deployment we need SOC2 certs, KMS integration, and proof of audit logs retention. last time we got a bundle but need specifics for VPC peering.
01:18 Jordan: totally, priya will send the SOC2 excerpt and the KMS integration guide after this call. we also have an updated private deployment checklist for VPC peering and audited logs.
01:28 Amir: perfect. also curious about data residency  if we add eu-west region does data stay in eu or is there a cross-region fallback?
01:37 Priya: routing policy can pin to eu for primary and fall back to us for failover; we can show routing policy config and the retention controls. there are options to keep all logs in-region if required under enterprise plan.
01:52 Marcus: on pricing  we got months left on contract, can we extend early to lock current rate if we add capacity? procurement team prefers that.
02:03 Jordan: yes we can do contract amendment to add committed capacity and extend term; i'll include that in the pricing sheet. there might be a pro-rated charge for the mid-cycle add.
02:16 Tess: how about benchmark  we want to run a 99th percentile latency test under our workload. what's involved?
02:24 Priya: we can run a short pilot on Dedicated  we provision a small reserved pool in eu-west, mirror subset of traffic, run for 24 hours. SE will instrument traces and produce a report with 50/95/99 latency plus cost per 1k tokens.
02:40 Marcus: realistic  and will that use our KV cache behavior? our workloads use prefix KV caching a lot.
02:46 Priya: yes we can simulate KV cache patterns, although kv cache might be imperfect in the pilot if we can't replicate full state; we'll call that out in the report.
02:58 Jordan: competitors  Anthropic or doing in-house?
03:05 Marcus: we've benchmarked in-house but ops cost is high; Anthropic was closer on latency but more expensive and less flexible on private deploy.
03:16 Jordan: good color. i'll include a short comparison note.
03:22 Amir: back to compliance  we need SSO/SAML and RBAC mapping documented for our IdP (Okta). will your private offer support SCIM?
03:31 Priya: yes SAML + SCIM is supported; we'll share the mapping guide. for RBAC we have per-route and token-level controls in the console.
03:43 Sofia: one small thing  autoscaling policies; how do we avoid cold-start latency when scaling up? our use-case is chatty short requests.
03:52 Priya: we have burst capacity and pre-warmed slots; also continuous batching tweaks and a keep-warm policy to reduce cold starts. we'll recommend config based on your sample load.
04:06 Marcus: timeline  procurement wants to lock things by 2026-09-20. is that feasible?
04:12 Jordan: yes, if we get signed amendment by the 20th we can schedule capacity and region provisioning in early october. i'll coordinate with ops.
04:24 Evan: one note on contract  multi-year discount is available for 12-24 month commits; that might help with sticker shock.
04:33 Tess: we'll take that back to procurement.
04:39 Priya: action: we'll set up the benchmark and send the security artifacts.
04:44 Marcus: ok appreciate it.

Action Items recap: Jordan to send pricing and contract amendment draft; Priya to send security docs and pilot checklist; Customer to share load sample and procurement window.

End of call.
